linkedin.documentTitle: The Repair or Replace Decision Framework
linkedin.text:
The repair-or-replace call is where a roofing contractor's incentives get tested, because one answer pays a few hundred dollars and the other pays five figures. After 10+ years on Portland metro roofs, we'd rather put the framework on the table so homeowners can run it without us in the room.

The short version: a roof under 15 years old with an isolated problem gets repaired, a roof past 20 with widespread issues gets replaced, and the middle comes down to three questions. Is the problem local or general (repairs can't fix general problems)? How much paid-for life is left (a $1,500 repair with ten good years left costs $150 a year; with two years left, $750 a year, and the replacement still comes)? And is this the first repair or the fourth? Worth knowing: the average leak call we take ends in a repair, not a replacement pitch.

For the genuinely torn cases, the advice is to buy information before buying anything else. A thorough assessment with photos turns vague worry into slope-by-slope facts, and ours is free. With Oregon's dry season here, this is the time to get the decision made on your schedule instead of the roof's.
